docs.title: Intent Disambiguation
docs.text:
This is the documentation site for the Intent Disambiguation service. The service is part of the wider DataGEMS platform.

DataGEMS lets users look for relevant datasets (cross-dataset discovery) or for facts computed from data (in-dataset discovery). The platform's home page has a single search box, so something has to decide which of the two a user meant. This service makes that decision: it reads the text the user typed and returns one of four intents, together with a keyword query for the discovery step.

Intent The user wants The platform should dataset_search to find or browse datasets run cross-dataset discovery question an answer computed from data find datasets with cross-dataset discovery, then run in-dataset discovery on them ambiguous either, it is not clear which ask the user which one they meant out_of_scope something that is not a data request show a short message and example queries

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• One call, one answer: a single LLM call with strict JSON-schema output returns the intent, a confidence and an English keyword query, in about 0.7 s.
  • Any language: inputs in Greek, Greeklish, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Polish are handled like English ones.
  • Conversation aware: optional context (selected datasets, earlier messages, the home-page topic filter) lets short follow-ups such as "and per month?" be read correctly.
  • Never blocks the home page: if the LLM is unavailable the service still answers, with ambiguous and degraded: true, so the UI falls back to asking the user.
  • Measured: an 876-input benchmark written and labelled by other model families tracks accuracy and misroutes per phrasing style, language and domain (see Evaluation).
  • Platform-native: DataGEMS AAI bearer tokens, the Gateway's x-tracking-correlation header, structured JSON logs and Kubernetes probes.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. The Gateway API forwards the user's text, and optionally the conversation context, to POST /api/v1/intent.
  2. The service validates the caller's token and renders a versioned prompt with the input.
  3. The SCAYLE-hosted LLM (qwen3.8-flash-next by default) answers in a fixed JSON schema.
  4. Labels below the confidence threshold become ambiguous; the keyword query is filled in or cleared depending on the intent.
  5. The Gateway runs the matching discovery flow and tells the UI which view to open (see the Integration Guide).

The service only classifies. It never calls cross-dataset or in-dataset discovery itself.

Not the same as query disambiguation

The Gateway's /api/search/disambiguate-query endpoint, served through the Task Orchestrator, rewrites unclear terms inside a query ("Zurich: the city or the canton?"). Intent disambiguation decides which flow should handle the query.

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text: The Intent Disambiguation service provides a small RESTful API: one endpoint that classifies an input, and endpoints for health monitoring. This page describes them; the full schema is on the OpenAPI page, and live documentation is served at /swagger and /redoc.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
When authentication is enabled (ENABLE_AUTH=true, the setting in every deployment), requests to the intent endpoint must include a token issued by the DataGEMS AAI:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

See Security for the checks applied to the token.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
https://{host}/dg-intent-disambiguation

Where {host} is the DataGEMS host, for example datagems-dev.scayle.es for the development environment. Inside the cluster the service is reachable at http://dg-intent-disambiguation-api-service.athenarc.svc.cluster.local:8000, without the path prefix.

docs.title: Classify an Input
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/intent

Decides whether the text a user typed asks for datasets or for an answer.

docs.title: Request Headers
docs.text: Header Required Description Authorization when auth is enabled Bearer <token> Content-Type yes application/json x-tracking-correlation no Correlation id; logged as DGCorrelationId and echoed in the response. Generated when missing.

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
{
  "query": "What was the mean temperature in Athens in 2020?",
  "context": {
    "domain": "weather",
    "dataset_ids": ["9b25bc46-8bd3-4f7f-94b4-52dbc38c130f"],
    "history": ["Show me the temperature datasets for Greece"]
  }
}
Field Type Required Description query string yes The text the user typed. 1 to 2000 characters after trimming; any language. context.domain string no The topic filter selected on the home page. At most 100 characters. context.dataset_ids array of UUIDs no Datasets already selected in the conversation. At most 200. context.history array of strings no Earlier user messages, oldest first. At most 10; the last 5 are used.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "intent": "question",
  "confidence": 0.95,
  "search_query": "mean temperature Athens 2020",
  "degraded": false,
  "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
  "prompt_version": "v2"
}
Field Type Description intent string dataset_search, question, ambiguous or out_of_scope. See Intent Classification. confidence number 0 to 1, reported by the model. Labels below the threshold have already been turned into ambiguous. search_query string or null English keywords for cross-dataset discovery. null only for out_of_scope. degraded boolean true when the model could not be used; the answer is then ambiguous with the raw input as search_query. model string The model that produced the answer. prompt_version string The prompt version that produced the answer.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST "https://{host}/dg-intent-disambiguation/api/v1/intent" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-tracking-correlation: 4f9c2a" \
  -d '{"query": "Do you have any data on air pollution in Athens?"}'

{
  "intent": "dataset_search",
  "confidence": 1.0,
  "search_query": "air pollution Athens",
  "degraded": false,
  "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
  "prompt_version": "v2"
}

Typical latency is about 0.7 s, and 1.1 s at the 95th percentile. Callers should set a timeout of about 30 s: the service's own call to SCAYLE times out after 20 s.

docs.title: Liveness
docs.text:
GET /

{"service": "dg-intent-disambiguation", "version": "0.2.0"}

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text:
GET /monitoring/ready

{"status": "ready"}

Does not depend on SCAYLE. See Maintenance.

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
GET /monitoring/health-check

Reports whether SCAYLE is reachable and the configured model is listed. Always returns 200 from a live pod; problems show up as status: degraded.

{
  "status": "healthy",
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "scayle": {"status": "healthy", "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next", "model_available": true}
}

docs.title: Service Architecture
docs.text: The Intent Disambiguation service is a small, stateless FastAPI application. It holds no database or queue: every request is answered by one call to an LLM hosted on SCAYLE.

docs.title: High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    UI[DataGEMS UI] --> GW[Gateway API]
    GW -- "POST /api/v1/intent<br/>exchanged token" --> ID[Intent Disambiguation]
    ID -- "chat completion<br/>(JSON schema)" --> LLM[SCAYLE LLM API]
    ID -. "signing keys (JWKS)" .-> AAI[DataGEMS AAI]
    GW -- dataset_search / question --> CDD[Cross-dataset discovery]
    GW -- question --> IDD[In-dataset discovery]

The Gateway owns the user-facing flow. It calls this service first, then runs the discovery flow that matches the returned intent, and tells the UI which view to open.

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
intent_disambiguation/main.py builds the FastAPI application:

  • POST /api/v1/intent classifies an input (routes/intent.py).
  • GET /, GET /monitoring/ready and GET /monitoring/health-check serve the Kubernetes probes and diagnostics (routes/health.py).
  • A middleware reads the x-tracking-correlation header (or creates an id), binds it to every log line as DGCorrelationId, echoes it in the response and writes one access log line per request.

Request and response models live in schemas.py. Validation errors are returned by FastAPI as 422 responses.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: auth.py validates DataGEMS AAI (Keycloak) bearer tokens: signature against the realm's published keys, issuer, expiry, and optionally audience and calling client. It is switched on with ENABLE_AUTH. See Security.

docs.title: Classifier
docs.text:
classifier.py turns an input into an answer:

  1. Loads the versioned prompt prompts/intent_<version>.yaml and renders its examples into the system message.
  2. Renders the user message: the input inside <input> tags, followed by an optional <context> block with the topic filter, the number of selected datasets and the last five earlier messages.
  3. Calls the LLM with temperature 0 and a strict JSON schema (intent, confidence, search_query).
  4. Parses and validates the answer, applies the confidence threshold and fixes up search_query.
  5. On any failure (connection, timeout, empty or invalid output) returns the degraded answer instead of an error.

See Intent Classification for the details.

docs.title: SCAYLE Client
docs.text:
llm/scayle.py is a small async client for the OpenAI-compatible SCAYLE API:

  • Exchanges the LDAP credentials for a bearer token (POST /v1/auths/ldap), caches it, and renews it once when a call returns 401.
  • Retries once on connection errors and on 502, 503 and 504.
  • Applies a connect timeout of 5 s and a read timeout of SCAYLE_TIMEOUT (20 s).
  • Sends chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking to switch the model's reasoning phase on or off.

Credentials are never logged or included in error messages.

docs.title: Request Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant GW as Gateway API
    participant ID as Intent Disambiguation
    participant AAI as DataGEMS AAI
    participant LLM as SCAYLE LLM
    GW->>ID: POST /api/v1/intent {query, context}
    ID->>AAI: fetch signing keys (cached for 1 h)
    ID->>ID: validate token, render prompt
    ID->>LLM: POST /chat/completions (JSON schema)
    alt answer received
        LLM-->>ID: {intent, confidence, search_query}
        ID->>ID: confidence threshold, fix search_query
        ID-->>GW: 200 {intent, ..., degraded: false}
    else LLM down, timeout or invalid output
        ID-->>GW: 200 {intent: ambiguous, ..., degraded: true}
    end

docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
• Classify only. Discovery calls, dataset filtering and the conversation stay in the Gateway, so this service has no state and can be scaled or replaced on its own.
  • Degrade, do not fail. An LLM outage turns into ambiguous answers rather than 5xx errors, so the home page keeps working and the user is asked to choose.
  • Thinking off by default. With reasoning enabled the model is about as accurate but four times slower at the tail, and long reasoning can exhaust the token budget (see Evaluation).
  • Prompts are data. Each prompt version is a YAML file, selected by PROMPT_VERSION, so a new prompt can be evaluated side by side with the current one before it is switched on.
  • No heavy dependencies. The image contains FastAPI, httpx, pydantic, structlog, PyJWT and PyYAML (about 230 MB) and starts in a couple of seconds.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The service is configured entirely through environment variables. For local runs they are read from a .env file (copy .env.example); in Kubernetes they come from the ConfigMap, and the credentials from a Vault-backed Secret (see Deployment).

No quotes in .env

Do not put quotes around values in .env: docker --env-file passes them through literally, and the SCAYLE login then fails with HTTP 400.

docs.title: Service
docs.text: Variable Default Description BASE_URL empty Path prefix the service is mounted under behind the ingress, e.g. /dg-intent-disambiguation. Used as the FastAPI root path, so /swagger works behind the prefix. LOG_LEVEL INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL. LOG_JSON false true writes JSON log lines, as in Kubernetes; false writes human-readable lines.

docs.title: SCAYLE LLM
docs.text: Variable Default Description SCAYLE_BASE_URL https://chat.scayle.es/api Base URL of the SCAYLE API. The development environment uses https://172.16.59.5:32443/api. SCAYLE_USERNAME LDAP user name. Secret. SCAYLE_PASSWORD LDAP password. Secret. SCAYLE_VERIFY_SSL true false for the development proxy, which uses a self-signed certificate. SCAYLE_TIMEOUT 20 Read timeout of one LLM call, in seconds. The connect timeout is 5 s.

docs.title: Classification
docs.text: Variable Default Description INTENT_MODEL qwen3.8-flash-next Model id. Ids are case sensitive and get renamed; /monitoring/health-check reports whether this one is listed. INTENT_ENABLE_THINKING false Let the model reason before answering. Slower, and reasoning counts against INTENT_MAX_TOKENS. INTENT_MAX_TOKENS 1024 Output token budget per call, including reasoning tokens. INTENT_MIN_CONFIDENCE 0.6 Labels other than ambiguous below this confidence are returned as ambiguous. PROMPT_VERSION v2 Selects intent_disambiguation/prompts/intent_<version>.yaml.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Variable Default Description ENABLE_AUTH false Require a DataGEMS AAI bearer token on the intent endpoint. true in every deployment. OIDC_ISSUER https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/oauth/realms/dev Expected token issuer. Signing keys are fetched from {OIDC_ISSUER}/protocol/openid-connect/certs. OIDC_AUDIENCE empty When set, the token's aud must contain this value. ALLOWED_CLIENTS empty Comma-separated client ids (azp) allowed to call the service. Empty allows any client with a valid token. OIDC_VERIFY_SSL true Verify the certificate of the AAI when fetching keys.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
With ENABLE_AUTH=true the service accepts tokens issued by the realm in OIDC_ISSUER. The Gateway API calls it with an exchanged token, whose azp claim names the Gateway's client. Once the Gateway's client id has been confirmed in the logs (it is logged as ClientId), set ALLOWED_CLIENTS to it so that only the Gateway can call the service.

See Security for the full list of checks and the resulting status codes.

docs.title: Development Environment Values
docs.text:
BASE_URL=/dg-intent-disambiguation
LOG_LEVEL=INFO
LOG_JSON=true
SCAYLE_BASE_URL=https://172.16.59.5:32443/api
SCAYLE_VERIFY_SSL=false
SCAYLE_TIMEOUT=20
INTENT_MODEL=qwen3.8-flash-next
INTENT_ENABLE_THINKING=false
INTENT_MAX_TOKENS=1024
INTENT_MIN_CONFIDENCE=0.6

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The service is part of the DataGEMS platform offered through an existing deployment, following the DataGEMS release and deployment procedures over a managed infrastructure. The purpose of this section is not to detail the deployment processes put in place by the DataGEMS team.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
The service is offered as a Docker image through the DataGEMS GitHub Organization Packages, as ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/dg-intent-disambiguation.

The image is built from the repository's Dockerfile:

  • based on python:3.11-slim-bookworm,
  • runtime dependencies installed with uv from the locked uv.lock, without development tools,
  • runs uvicorn intent_disambiguation.main:app on port 8000 as an unprivileged user (uid 10001),
  • works with a read-only root filesystem.

Build and publication are handled by the .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml GitHub Actions workflow, which is triggered when a v* tag is pushed (i.e. on new releases). The image tag matches the git tag.

To run the image locally:

make docker-run   # builds the image and runs it with the settings in .env

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
The Kubernetes manifests are kept in two deployment repositories, dg-intent-disambiguation-deployment-dev and dg-intent-disambiguation-deployment-prod, applied with kustomize. Each has a deploy script that refuses to run against the other environment's cluster; the prod script also asks for typed confirmation. In the development environment the service runs in the athenarc namespace as:

Resource Name Deployment dg-intent-disambiguation-api (1 replica, 128 Mi / 100 m requested, 512 Mi / 500 m limit) Service dg-intent-disambiguation-api-service, port 8000 Ingress and HTTPRoute path prefix /dg-intent-disambiguation, rewritten to / ConfigMap dg-intent-disambiguation-api-config, the settings described in Configuration VaultStaticSecret creates dg-intent-disambiguation-app-secrets from the Vault path athenarc/dg-intent-disambiguation

The pod resolves the AAI host name (datagems-dev.scayle.es) to the ingress controller through hostAliases, so that it can fetch the token signing keys from inside the cluster.

docs.title: Probes
docs.text:
Neither probe depends on SCAYLE. When the LLM is down the intent endpoint still answers (degraded), so the pod must stay in the Service:

Probe Endpoint Liveness GET / Readiness GET /monitoring/ready

GET /monitoring/health-check reports SCAYLE status for diagnostics only. See Maintenance.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: In order for the service to operate properly, the needed configuration values must be set to match the environment that it must operate in. The needed configuration is described in the relevant Configuration section.

docs.title: Status & Error Codes
docs.text: This page documents the status codes returned by the Intent Disambiguation API and how failures of the underlying LLM are reported.

docs.title: HTTP Status Codes
Degraded Answers
docs.text:
The intent endpoint never turns an LLM problem into an error status. When the SCAYLE API cannot be reached, times out, rejects the request, or returns an empty or invalid answer, the response is 200 with:

Field Value intent ambiguous confidence 0.0 degraded true search_query the raw input

Callers handle it like any ambiguous answer: ask the user whether they want datasets or an answer. The cause is logged as a warning (Intent model unavailable, falling back to ambiguous), and /monitoring/health-check shows whether SCAYLE is reachable.

docs.title: Health Status Values
docs.text: Value Endpoint Meaning ready /monitoring/ready The process serves requests. healthy /monitoring/health-check SCAYLE is reachable and the configured model is listed. degraded /monitoring/health-check SCAYLE is unreachable, or the configured model is not listed (model ids are case sensitive and get renamed). The scayle.message field explains which.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
The classifier is measured on two labelled sets in the repository's eval/ folder. Both run against the real model, so they need access to SCAYLE.

Set Inputs Purpose Command Regression set (eval/queries.yaml) 134 Written alongside the prompt; checks that known cases keep working make eval Benchmark (eval/benchmark/benchmark.jsonl) 876 Independent measurement: written and labelled by other model families, reviewed by hand make benchmark

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
• Accuracy: share of inputs with exactly the expected intent, over the inputs that have a single expected intent.
  • Misroutes: errors that send the user to the wrong place: a dataset search answered as a question or the other way round, or a data request marked out_of_scope. Answering ambiguous for a clear input is not a misroute: it costs the user one click.
  • Contested inputs: inputs on which reasonable people would pick different flows (questions about a dataset's licence, general-knowledge questions, requests for learning material, bare keywords the annotators disagreed on). Each has a list of acceptable intents and is reported separately.
  • Degraded: answers produced by the fallback because the model failed.
  • Latency: median and 95th percentile per request.

The report also breaks accuracy down by phrasing style, language and domain, and lists every error.

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text:
The benchmark was built in three stages by eval/benchmark/build_benchmark.py:

  1. Generate. 198 recipes cross the intent with a phrasing style, a domain, a language and a kind of noise. DeepSeek-V4-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash on SCAYLE write the inputs in turn. Neither is the Qwen model under test. The recipes are grounded in the datasets the platform hosts (Greek weather stations, ERA5-Land, cement CO2 emissions, BioTIME, the Britannica, Diderot and EncycNet encyclopedias, MathE, CEDEFOP, ESCO, ISCO, last-mile delivery) and in topics it does not host.
  2. Judge. Both models label every input from an annotation guide written separately from the production prompt.
  3. Review. An input is accepted when both judges agree with the intent it was generated for. The remaining 163 inputs were reviewed by hand; every decision and its reason is recorded in eval/benchmark/overrides.yaml.

docs.title: Composition
docs.text:
Group Inputs English phrasing styles across 7 domains, including 8 kinds of out-of-scope input and prompt injection 512 Greek, Greeklish, Greek-English mix, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish (20 each) 180 Noise: typos, long and rambling, terse, all caps and emojis 96 Follow-ups with earlier messages and selected datasets 40 Contested by design 48

679 inputs have a single expected intent (question 289, dataset_search 205, ambiguous 97, out_of_scope 88) and 197 are contested. The two judges agree with each other on 87% of the non-contested inputs: the line between ambiguous and the other intents is fuzzy for keyword inputs, which is why misroutes matter more than accuracy.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Measured on 2 November 2026 with qwen3.8-flash-next:

Configuration Strict accuracy Misroutes Contested Degraded Prompt v2, thinking off (deployed) 96.5% 2 97.5% 0 Prompt v1 (with reason), thinking off 96.5% 4 98.5% 0 Prompt v1, thinking on 96.9% 0 96.4% 31 Rules candidate (not kept), thinking off 95.1% 3 97.5% 0

Latency, measured one request at a time on 120 benchmark inputs, alternating the two prompts so that both see the same load:

Prompt Median Mean p95 v2 (deployed) 715 ms 756 ms 1142 ms v1 (with reason) 819 ms 921 ms 1569 ms

Under the same parallel load, thinking on was about 1.7 times slower at the median and four times slower at p95 than thinking off.

Prompt v1 asked for a one-sentence reason before the label, so that the model would explain itself first. It did not pay for itself: v2 drops it and keeps the accuracy, with fewer misroutes and a shorter tail.

With the deployed configuration:

  • Per intent, precision / recall: dataset_search 95.2 / 97.1, question 99.3 / 97.9, ambiguous 89.6 / 88.7, out_of_scope 97.8 / 98.9.
  • Every English phrasing style, the 7 domains, the 8 kinds of out-of-scope input (including prompt injection) and French, German, Greek and Greek-English are at 95 to 100%. Greeklish is lowest at 85%, then Spanish, Italian and Portuguese at 90%, on 20 inputs each.
  • The regression set scores 100% with no misroutes.
  • The 2 misroutes: a REST API question about ESCO that the judges labelled dataset_search and the model answered out of scope, and a Polish request for the occurrences of a word that the model read as a dataset search.

With thinking on, 31 replies ran out of the token budget while still reasoning and fell back to the degraded answer. The rules candidate added prompt rules for the error patterns below; it moved errors between intents rather than removing them, so it was not kept.

docs.title: Known Weak Spots
docs.text:
• Learning material ("I need video tutorials on linear algebra", "MATHE INTEGRATION BY PARTS EXERCISES") is sometimes marked out_of_scope. Whether such requests should go to dataset search or to the MathE recommendation endpoint is still to be decided.
  • Questions about a dataset itself (licence, API, citation) do not fit the four intents cleanly; one of the two misroutes is of this kind.
  • One-word follow-ups after a question ("precipitation"), terse value phrases ("average July temperature Heraklion 2019") and keywords naming a dataset ("ERA5-Land soil moisture France 2005") are often answered ambiguous. These cost the user one extra click.

docs.title: Running the Evaluation
docs.text:
make eval        # regression set
make benchmark   # benchmark, about 5 minutes

# compare settings without changing the deployment
uv run --env-file .env python eval/run_eval.py \
    --queries eval/benchmark/benchmark.jsonl --prompt-version v2 --thinking

# evaluate a deployed instance
uv run python eval/run_eval.py --url https://{host}/dg-intent-disambiguation/api/v1/intent \
    --token "$TOKEN"

# re-score stored predictions after relabelling, without calling the model
uv run python eval/run_eval.py --queries eval/benchmark/benchmark.jsonl \
    --reuse eval/results/eval-<stamp>.json

Every run writes the full set of answers to eval/results/.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: This document answers frequently asked questions about the Intent Disambiguation service.

docs.title: What is the Intent Disambiguation service?
docs.text: A service that reads what a user typed into the DataGEMS search box and decides whether they want to find datasets, get an answer computed from data, either of the two, or something that is not a data request. The Gateway API uses the answer to pick the discovery flow and the view to open.

docs.title: Does it search for datasets or answer questions itself?
docs.text: No. It only classifies the input and returns a keyword query. The Gateway runs cross-dataset discovery and in-dataset discovery.

docs.title: How is it different from the Gateway's query disambiguation?
docs.text: The Gateway's /api/search/disambiguate-query endpoint rewrites unclear terms inside a query for a chosen set of datasets. Intent disambiguation runs earlier and decides which flow should handle the query at all.

docs.title: Which languages are supported?
docs.text: Any language the model understands. The benchmark covers English, Greek, Greeklish, mixed Greek and English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Polish. The search_query is always in English.

docs.title: Which model does it use?
docs.text: qwen3.8-flash-next on SCAYLE by default, with its reasoning phase switched off. The model is set with INTENT_MODEL.

docs.title: How fast is it?
docs.text: About 0.7 s per request, and 1.1 s at the 95th percentile, measured one request at a time on benchmark inputs.

docs.title: What happens when SCAYLE is down?
docs.text: The endpoint still answers 200 with intent: ambiguous and degraded: true, so the UI asks the user to choose. See Degraded Answers.

docs.title: Why do I get ambiguous for a clear request?
docs.text: Either the model's confidence was below INTENT_MIN_CONFIDENCE, or the answer is degraded (check the degraded field), or the input is a bare topic or keyword phrase, which the service deliberately leaves to the user. Short keyword inputs that name a dataset or ask for a value are a known weak spot; see Evaluation.

docs.title: Why does the response not explain its decision?
docs.text: An explanation costs generation time. Prompt v1 returned a one-sentence reason; dropping it made answers about 100 ms faster at the median and 430 ms at the 95th percentile, with the same accuracy. The confidence field and the logs are the diagnostics now.

docs.title: Can I send the conversation so far?
docs.text: Yes, as context.history and context.dataset_ids. Short follow-ups such as "and per month?" are then classified using the earlier messages, and search_query is completed from them.

docs.title: Is the input stored?
docs.text: No. The service is stateless, and inputs are logged only at DEBUG level. See Logging.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• Requests for mathematics learning material are sometimes classified out_of_scope.
  • Questions about a dataset's licence, API or citation do not fit the four intents cleanly.
  • The question flow needs in-dataset discovery to accept the selected dataset ids, which the Gateway does not forward yet.

docs.title: Integrating intent disambiguation
docs.text:
For the Gateway API and the UI. The service answers one question about what a user typed into the home-page search box: do they want datasets or an answer?

The full endpoint reference is in the API Overview; this page covers how to use the answer.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
POST {base}/api/v1/intent
Environment {base} Dev, in cluster http://dg-intent-disambiguation-api-service.athenarc.svc.cluster.local:8000 Dev, public https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/dg-intent-disambiguation

Swagger: https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/dg-intent-disambiguation/swagger

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: Header Authorization: Bearer <token> Token issued by the DataGEMS AAI (dev realm). The exchanged token the Gateway uses for other services works. x-tracking-correlation Optional. Logged as DGCorrelationId and echoed back.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
{
  "query": "What was the mean temperature in Athens in 2020?",
  "context": {
    "domain": "weather",
    "dataset_ids": ["9b25bc46-8bd3-4f7f-94b4-52dbc38c130f"],
    "history": ["Earlier user message"]
  }
}
  • query: required, 1 to 2000 characters, any language.
  • context: optional; every field is optional. It is passed to the model as a hint:
  • domain: the topic filter the user picked on the home page, if any.
  • dataset_ids: datasets already selected in the conversation. With datasets selected, short follow-ups ("and per month?") are read as questions about them.
  • history: earlier user messages, oldest first; the last 5 are used.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "intent": "question",
  "confidence": 0.95,
  "search_query": "mean temperature Athens 2020",
  "degraded": false,
  "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
  "prompt_version": "v2"
}
Field intent dataset_search, question, ambiguous or out_of_scope confidence 0 to 1, reported by the model. Labels below 0.6 are already turned into ambiguous. search_query English keywords for cross-dataset discovery. null only for out_of_scope. degraded true when the model could not be reached. The answer is then ambiguous with the raw input as search_query. model, prompt_version What produced the answer, for logs and comparisons.

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
Code When 200 Always when the request is valid, including when the model is down (degraded: true) 401 Missing, expired or invalid token 403 The calling client is not on the allow list 422 Invalid body (blank or overlong query, malformed dataset_ids) 503 The AAI keys could not be fetched to check the token

Latency is about 0.7 s typical and 1.1 s at the 95th percentile. Set a client timeout of about 30 s: the service's own call to SCAYLE times out after 20 s.

docs.title: Suggested routing
docs.text:
Intent Gateway UI dataset_search Run cross-dataset discovery with search_query Datasets page, smart search box filled with the user's text, results below question Run cross-dataset discovery with search_query, take the top datasets, then run in-dataset discovery with the original query on them Chat with those datasets pre-selected and the answer. Offer "show me the datasets instead" ambiguous Nothing yet Ask: "Find datasets about this" or "Get an answer". Then follow the chosen row above out_of_scope Nothing A short message and the example queries

Notes:

  • search_query is for retrieval only. Show the user their own text, and give in-dataset discovery the original question: keywords drop words that matter for answering ("mean", "per month").
  • The UI should always let the user switch between the dataset and answer flows, because the model can be wrong.
  • question depends on in-dataset discovery accepting dataset ids. Today the Gateway's in-data-explore call forwards only the question.

docs.title: Suggested Gateway configuration
docs.text:
Following the existing service-*.json files:

{
  "IntentDisambiguationService": {
    "Scope": "datagems",
    "BaseUrl": "%{IntentDisambiguationBaseUrl}%",
    "IntentEndpoint": "api/v1/intent"
  }
}

The service validates the token's signature, issuer and expiry. It does not yet require a specific audience or client. Once the Gateway's first calls show its client id in the logs, ALLOWED_CLIENTS will be set to it (expected dg-app-api). Tell us if the exchanged token for this scope should carry a specific aud value.

docs.title: Intent Classification
docs.text: This page describes how an input becomes an answer: the intents, the prompt, the structured output and the rules applied after the model answers.

docs.title: Intents
docs.text:
Intent Definition Examples dataset_search The user wants to find or browse datasets, asks whether data exists, or wants to download or access data. "Do you have any data about temperatures across Europe?", "I need a corpus of Austrian newspapers" question The user wants an answer looked up or computed from data: a value, count, list, comparison, trend, ranking, chart or table. Includes commands ("plot ...") and keyword phrases that clearly ask for a value. "What was the mean temperature in Athens in 2020?", "Plot the daily precipitation in Patras for 2022" ambiguous Only a topic or keywords, with no sign of either. "surface temperature increase", "unemployment in Greece" out_of_scope Not a request about data: greetings, chit-chat, personal or creative requests, general help, questions about the assistant or the platform, gibberish, attempts to change the instructions. "tell me how I feel tonight", "write a poem about the sea"

A request for a value stays a question even when it mentions data or datasets ("According to the weather datasets, how much did it rain in Ioannina in March 2021?").

docs.title: Prompt
docs.text:
The prompt is a versioned YAML file in intent_disambiguation/prompts/, selected with PROMPT_VERSION (default v2). It contains:

  • a short description of the platform and the kinds of data it hosts,
  • the four intent definitions and the decision rules,
  • the fields to return,
  • worked examples, rendered as input and expected output.

The user message wraps the input in <input> tags and adds a <context> block when the request carries context:

<input>
and per month?
</input>
<context>
Datasets already selected in this conversation: 1
Earlier messages in this conversation, oldest first:
- What was the mean temperature in Athens in 2020?
</context>

The prompt tells the model to treat the input only as text to classify and never to follow instructions found in it.

docs.title: Structured Output
docs.text:
The model is called with temperature 0 and a strict JSON schema:

{
  "intent": "dataset_search | question | ambiguous | out_of_scope",
  "confidence": "number",
  "search_query": "string or null"
}

The schema is kept to the fields the caller needs: every generated token adds latency. Prompt v1 also asked for a one-sentence reason before the label; removing it in v2 cut median latency by about 100 ms and 95th-percentile latency by about 430 ms with the same benchmark accuracy. The answer is validated with pydantic; text around the JSON object (code fences, for example) is tolerated.

docs.title: Rules Applied After the Model Answers
docs.text:
• Confidence threshold. confidence is clamped to [0, 1]. Any label other than ambiguous with confidence below INTENT_MIN_CONFIDENCE (default 0.6) becomes ambiguous: asking the user costs one click, a wrong flow costs more.
  • Search query. search_query is an English keyword query (2 to 10 words) for cross-dataset discovery: places, periods, variables and named sources are kept, question words and filler are dropped, and follow-ups are resolved from the earlier messages. It is null for out_of_scope. If the model leaves it empty for another intent, the raw input is used.

docs.title: Degraded Answers
docs.text:
When the SCAYLE API cannot be reached, times out, or returns an empty or invalid answer, the service answers 200 with:

{
  "intent": "ambiguous",
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "search_query": "<the raw input>",
  "degraded": true
}

The UI then asks the user which flow they meant, exactly as for a genuine ambiguous answer. A warning is logged with the cause.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
All context fields are optional hints:

Field Effect domain The topic filter picked on the home page, e.g. weather. dataset_ids Datasets already selected. With datasets selected and an earlier question, a short follow-up is read as a question about them. Only the count is sent to the model. history Earlier user messages, oldest first. The last five are sent; they are also used to complete search_query for follow-ups.

docs.title: Thinking Mode
docs.text: Qwen models can reason before answering. It is switched off by default (INTENT_ENABLE_THINKING=false, sent as chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking): on the benchmark it removed the last few misroutes but quadrupled tail latency, and reasoning tokens count against INTENT_MAX_TOKENS, so a long reasoning phase can end without an answer. See Evaluation.

docs.title: Changing the Prompt
docs.text:
1. Add prompts/intent_v3.yaml. Keep its examples out of the evaluation sets.
  2. Run the evaluation with --prompt-version v3 on the regression set and the benchmark, and compare with v2. Look at misroutes as well as accuracy.
  3. Switch with PROMPT_VERSION=v3 in the deployment configuration. The response's prompt_version field shows which prompt produced each answer.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: This document describes the logging of the Intent Disambiguation service.

docs.title: Logging System
docs.text: The service uses structured logging based on the Python structlog library, configured in intent_disambiguation/logging_setup.py. Logs from the service, from uvicorn and from httpx all go through the same formatter and are written to standard output.

docs.title: Log Formats
docs.text: LOG_JSON Format Used in true One JSON object per line Kubernetes false Human-readable, coloured lines Local development

docs.title: Log Levels
docs.text:
Level Description DEBUG Detailed information, including the user's input and the generated search query INFO One line per handled request and per classification WARNING Degraded answers, rejected tokens, disallowed clients ERROR The AAI signing keys could not be fetched

The default level is INFO, set with LOG_LEVEL. httpx request lines are kept at WARNING so that the SCAYLE login is not logged.

docs.title: Request Context
docs.text:
Every line written while handling a request carries these fields, using the same names as the Gateway API's log tracking so that the two can be joined:

Field Source DGCorrelationId The x-tracking-correlation request header, or a generated UUID when it is missing or invalid. Also returned in the response header. ClientId The token's azp (or client_id) claim, when authentication is enabled UserId The token's sub claim, when authentication is enabled

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Event Level Fields Starting Intent Disambiguation Service INFO version, root_path, model, thinking, prompt_version, auth Request handled INFO method, path, status, latency_ms. Not written for / and /monitoring/ready, which the probes call every few seconds. Intent classified INFO intent, model_intent (before the confidence threshold), confidence, query_length, latency_ms Intent input DEBUG query, search_query Intent model unavailable, falling back to ambiguous WARNING error, latency_ms Token rejected WARNING reason, status Client not allowed WARNING client_id Cannot fetch the identity provider keys ERROR error Health check completed INFO report

Example, with LOG_JSON=true:

{"intent": "question", "model_intent": "question", "confidence": 1.0, "query_length": 48, "latency_ms": 631, "event": "Intent classified", "DGCorrelationId": "demo-123", "logger": "dg-intent-disambiguation", "level": "info", "timestamp": "2026-10-30T13:26:56.344079Z"}

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: User inputs are not stored. At the default INFO level only their length is logged; the text itself appears only at DEBUG. SCAYLE credentials and bearer tokens are never logged.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text: This document provides guidance on checking the health of the Intent Disambiguation service and on the routine tasks that keep it working.

docs.title: Liveness and Readiness Probes
docs.text:
Both probes are pure HTTP and do not depend on SCAYLE, so an LLM outage never takes the pod out of the Service; the intent endpoint answers with degraded results instead.

curl -X GET "https://{host}/dg-intent-disambiguation/"
curl -X GET "https://{host}/dg-intent-disambiguation/monitoring/ready"

Expected responses:

{"service": "dg-intent-disambiguation", "version": "0.2.0"}
{"status": "ready"}

docs.title: Dependency Health Check
docs.text:
Reports whether SCAYLE is reachable and the configured model is listed. It is purely diagnostic: it always returns HTTP 200 from a live pod and reports problems in the body.

curl -X GET "https://{host}/dg-intent-disambiguation/monitoring/health-check"

Expected response:

{
  "status": "healthy",
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "scayle": {"status": "healthy", "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next", "model_available": true}
}

When SCAYLE is unreachable, or the model is no longer listed, status becomes degraded and scayle.message explains why.

docs.title: The Model Was Renamed or Removed
docs.text: SCAYLE model ids are case sensitive and are renamed from time to time. When /monitoring/health-check reports model_available: false, every answer is degraded. List the available models, pick the replacement, set INTENT_MODEL in the ConfigMap and restart the deployment. Run the evaluation with --model <id> before switching to a different model family.

docs.title: Degraded Answers
docs.text: Count the Intent model unavailable, falling back to ambiguous warnings in the logs. Their error field shows the cause: connection errors (SCAYLE or the VPN route down), HTTP 401 after renewal (credentials changed in Vault), or finish_reason=length (the token budget is too small, usually because thinking was switched on).

docs.title: Changing the Prompt
docs.text: Add a new prompt version, compare it with the current one on the regression set and the benchmark, and switch with PROMPT_VERSION. See Intent Classification and Evaluation.

docs.title: Tightening Authentication
docs.text: Once the Gateway's client id has been confirmed in the logs (ClientId), set ALLOWED_CLIENTS to it. See Configuration.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
1. Bump version in pyproject.toml and intent_disambiguation/__init__.py.
  2. Push a tag vX.Y.Z. The Docker publish workflow builds and pushes ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/dg-intent-disambiguation:vX.Y.Z.
  3. Update the image tag in the deployment repository and apply it.
  4. Publish the documentation for the new version with the Deploy Docs workflow.

docs.title: Security Scans
docs.text:
The repository offers on-demand GitHub Actions workflows, started from the Actions tab:

Workflow What it does CodeQL Scan (On-Demand) Static analysis of the Python code and the workflow files Vulnerability Scan (On-Demand) Trivy scan of the Dockerfile configuration and of a published image tag (critical and high findings) Code Metrics (On-Demand) Maintainability index, cyclomatic complexity and lines of code with radon

Each uploads its report as a workflow artifact (CodeQL results go to the repository's Security tab).

docs.title: DataGEMS Intent Disambiguation 0.2.0
docs.text: Decides whether text typed into the DataGEMS search box asks for datasets (cross-dataset discovery) or for an answer (in-dataset discovery), and returns a keyword query for the discovery step.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/intent
docs.text:
Decide whether the input asks for datasets or for an answer

Description

Classify the text a user typed into the home-page search box.

  • dataset_search: the user wants to find datasets; run cross-dataset discovery.
  • question: the user wants an answer; find datasets with cross-dataset discovery, then run in-dataset discovery on them.
  • ambiguous: both are plausible; ask the user which one they meant.
  • out_of_scope: not a data request.

search_query is an English keyword version of the input for cross-dataset discovery. When the model is unavailable the service still answers with ambiguous, degraded: true and the raw input as search_query, so callers can fall back to asking the user.

Input parameters

Parameter In Type Default Nullable Description HTTPBearer header string N/A No JWT Bearer token

Request body

application/json 

{
    "query": "What was the mean temperature in Athens in 2020?"
}
⚠️ This example has been generated automatically from the schema and it is not accurate. Refer to the schema for more information.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: This page summarizes the security-relevant aspects of the Intent Disambiguation service.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The intent endpoint accepts bearer tokens issued by the DataGEMS AAI (Keycloak). Authentication is switched on with ENABLE_AUTH=true, which is the setting in every deployment; with ENABLE_AUTH=false (the default for local runs) the endpoint is open.

When enabled, each request to POST /api/v1/intent must carry:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The token is accepted only if all of these checks pass:

Check Detail Signature Verified against the realm's published keys ({OIDC_ISSUER}/protocol/openid-connect/certs), cached for one hour. Only asymmetric algorithms are accepted (RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, ES256); a token signed with a shared secret is rejected. Issuer iss must equal OIDC_ISSUER. Expiry exp is required and checked, with 30 seconds of leeway. Audience aud must contain OIDC_AUDIENCE, when that setting is not empty. Calling client azp (or client_id) must be in ALLOWED_CLIENTS, when that setting is not empty.

The Gateway API calls the service with the token-exchange flow, as it does for other DataGEMS services, so the token represents the original user and the Gateway as the calling client.

Outcome Status Missing token, bad signature, wrong issuer or audience, expired 401 Unauthorized Valid token from a client not in ALLOWED_CLIENTS 403 Forbidden Signing keys cannot be fetched from the AAI 503 Service Unavailable

The health and documentation endpoints (/, /monitoring/*, /swagger, /redoc, /openapi.json) do not require a token.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text: The service is deployed behind the DataGEMS ingress, which terminates TLS. Inside the cluster it is reached over plain HTTP on port 8000. See Deployment.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: The only secrets are the SCAYLE credentials (SCAYLE_USERNAME, SCAYLE_PASSWORD). In Kubernetes they come from the Vault path athenarc/dg-intent-disambiguation, through the Vault operator, as the Secret dg-intent-disambiguation-app-secrets. They are never logged and never included in error messages. For local runs they live in an untracked .env file.

docs.title: Input Handling
docs.text:
• The input is limited to 2000 characters, the history to 10 messages and the selected datasets to 200 ids; larger requests are rejected with 422.
  • The prompt places the input inside <input> tags and instructs the model to treat it only as text to classify. The model can only answer through the fixed JSON schema, so an injected instruction can at worst change the returned label. Prompt-injection inputs are part of the benchmark and are classified out_of_scope.
  • The service does not store inputs. They appear in logs only at DEBUG level; at the default INFO level only the input length is logged.
  • Invalid correlation ids (anything other than 1 to 128 letters, digits, ., _, : or -) are replaced, so the header cannot inject content into the logs.

docs.title: Container
docs.text: The image is based on python:3.11-slim-bookworm, contains only the locked runtime dependencies, and runs as an unprivileged user (uid 10001). The Kubernetes deployment also sets a read-only root filesystem, drops all capabilities and disallows privilege escalation. The image can be scanned with the on-demand vulnerability scan workflow (see Maintenance).
